details: Asteroid Rush 3D is a browser game built in two halves that mirror how real missions work: first you design the mission, then you fly it. Players configure a spacecraft for a real NASA destination — engine, shielding, scanner — and then pilot it at full speed through the asteroid belt between Earth and that world, threading rocks, chasing near-miss combos, and hauling data orbs home as science. How it works: (1) Choose a destination — the Moon, Mars, asteroid 16 Psyche, and Jupiter's moon Europa, each with its real distance, travel time and a NASA fact. Runs get longer, faster and denser as you progress; completing one unlocks the next. (2) Design the mission — three real spacecraft decisions, each a genuine engineering trade-off: Engine: ChemPro (balanced), Nuclear Thermal (1.28x speed, 0.78x steering — real fission propulsion trades agility for thrust), Ion Surveyor (slow, precise, science x1.6). Shielding: Basic, Reinforced Plating, or a Whipple shield — the actual layered debris armor flown on the ISS and deep-space spacecraft — trading hull size against damage per hit. Scanner: Standard, a Magnet Array that pulls data orbs in, or a Science Array that doubles orb value. (3) Fly the rush — real-time 3D flight (Three.js) with speed that ramps through the run. Asteroid hits cost hull based on your shielding choice; near misses build a combo multiplier; data orbs are magnetized by your scanner. Your design choices are felt in your hands, not just read in a menu. (4) Progression — banked science buys permanent upgrades (hull plating, reinforced frame, magnet coil, engine tuning), so each attempt makes the next mission more survivable — the same iterate-and-improve loop real mission teams live by. NASA connection: Every destination is a real NASA mission target with a real fact card: Artemis and lunar south-pole water ice; Perseverance's Jezero sample tubes; the Psyche mission to a metal world (launched 2023, arriving 2029); Europa Clipper and the subsurface ocean (launched 2024). The design layer teaches real mission-design thinking — propulsion trade-offs, debris shielding, and instrument selection — through play, not lectures. Technology: Hand-written HTML/CSS/JavaScript with Three.js for real-time 3D (procedural spacecraft, procedural planet textures, pooled asteroids/orbs/particles, speed streaks and dynamic FOV for velocity feel). All sound is synthesized live with WebAudio — the engine hum tracks your speed; there are no audio files. The 2026 redesign adds a deep-space glass interface, a cinematic 3-2-1 countdown, an in-canvas HUD (hull, science, combo and a live distance track) visible in fullscreen, hitstop and FOV-kick feedback on near misses, and adaptive quality scaling so it stays smooth on low-end phones as well as desktops. It runs in any modern phone or desktop browser — no install, no login. Built by Abu Sufyan (BS Software Engineering, Riphah International University, Sahiwal), team MISSION UNSTOPPABLE!!
